reports.name: Q.Sb.bisa-1A
reports.note: 139 advanced CIMMYT spring wheat lines, GBS SNPs called on RefSeq v1.0, FarmCPU GWAS; Env1 Pusa 2019, Env2 Pusa 2020 (India), Env3 BARI Jamalpur 2017 (Bangladesh), natural infection; P < 0.003 in Table 2. The paper gives allele effects on disease severity (marker effect and "Effect 10X"), not PVE. Significant in Env1, Env2; peak SNP S1A_497201550; MAF 0.28. Allele effect: C allele +1.88 (Effect 10X 18.83) in Env1, +1.83 in Env2. Both SNPs lie 9.4 kb from TraesCS1A01G303600 (LURP-one-like protein); TraesCS1A01G303700 (GTP cyclohydrolase 1) 23 kb away. Reported as a new QTL. Earlier record lacked markers and effects. Re-read from the paper, Nov 2026 (ad61.py). Pangenome positions added Nov 2026 (ad64) with genome-wide gene anchors (106,795 Chinese Spring genes matched to each cultivar).

reports.name: Q.Sb.bisa-2B
reports.note: 139 advanced CIMMYT spring wheat lines, GBS SNPs called on RefSeq v1.0, FarmCPU GWAS; Env1 Pusa 2019, Env2 Pusa 2020 (India), Env3 BARI Jamalpur 2017 (Bangladesh), natural infection; P < 0.003 in Table 2. The paper gives allele effects on disease severity (marker effect and "Effect 10X"), not PVE. Significant in Env1, Env2, Env3; peak SNP S2B_422983662; MAF 0.11 (S2B_422983662); 0.45-0.46 (Env3 SNPs). reports.name: FHB resistance gene linked to B1 (Sumai 3)

reports.name: Pch1 (European winter wheat; fine-mapping)

reports.name: Eyespot QTL region 2AS (European winter wheat)
reports.note: GWAS for eyespot (field tests in three environments) in 168 European winter and 3 spring wheat varieties with 732 SSRs and 7,761 mapped 90K SNPs; 108 SSR and 235 SNP MTAs (-log10P 3.0 or more). SSR and SNP data indicated a QTL region on 2AS supported by numerous markers, most alleles reducing eyespot score (smaller effects than Pch1); proposed as a novel resistance source. Online Resource 3 lists the SSRs WMS0830 (15.4 cM, -log10P up to 4.58, R2 9.8%), WMS0636 (37.3 cM, 4.30, 9.5%) and WMS0359 (52.4 cM, 3.23, 7.9%), each with an allele that reduces eyespot (WMS0830 null, WMS0636 106, WMS0359 215). Xgwm830 could not be placed. Marker positions (RefSeq v1.0): Xgwm636 4.977 Mb (in-silico PCR); Xgwm359 28.205 Mb (in-silico PCR). Online Resource 4B lists 44 SNPs at 0.8, 4, 10.5, 28.1 cM (strongest Tdurum_contig63196_123, -log10P 5.28, R2 12.2%); 42 of 44 with the minor allele reducing eyespot. 22 SNPs placed in silico at 2.641-36.041 Mb (RefSeq v1.0; Hu et al. 2022 BMC Plant Biol (90K on v2.1); Sun et al. 2020 PBJ (90K)). The 10.5 cM block (37 SNPs, the peak of the region) places at 11.910-17.657 Mb. SSR data from Online Resource 3 (ad51.py); SNP data from Online Resource 4B, Nov 2026 (ad54.py). reports.name: Fhb1 (CM82036; MAS vs phenotypic selection)

reports.name: Fhb1 (combined with Sr2)
reports.note: Of 1,949 F2 plants screened with Xgwm533 and csSr2 (Sr2) and UMN10/UMN10v2 (Fhb1), 43 had Fhb1 and Sr2 in coupling; 59 homozygous F3 spring lines carrying both had significantly lower FHB severity and moderate to high stem rust resistance in field nurseries. Placed at the cloned Fhb1 (TaHRC) position in the atlas. Read from the paper, Nov 2026 (ad39.py). Pangenome positions added Nov 2026 (ad64) with genome-wide gene anchors (106,795 Chinese Spring genes matched to each cultivar).

reports.name: Qcrs.cpi-3B (CSCR6; pyramiding)
reports.note: Pyramiding of three large-effect crown rot QTL in two populations (EGA Wylie//Lang/CSCR6, 178 lines; EGA Wylie/Sumai3 x CSCR6 derived, 181 F8 lines), seedling assays in four trials; lines with two resistant alleles beat those with one or none, and lines with all three were most resistant. Resistant allele from T. spelta CSCR6 reduced disease index by 25.5-28.5%. Placed at the Qcrs.cpi-3B interval in the atlas. Read from the paper, Nov 2026 (ad39.py). Pangenome positions added Nov 2026 (ad64) with genome-wide gene anchors (106,795 Chinese Spring genes matched to each cultivar).

reports.name: Fhb1 = HisR/TaHRC (PFT not required)
reports.note: Lines carrying HisR (TaHRC) with or without PFT, and five HisR-carrying PFT mutants made by gene editing, showed that PFT does not confer FHB resistance and that the HisR effect does not require PFT; PFT mutations were not associated with morphological or phenological traits. This argues against PFT as the Fhb1 gene (Rawat et al. 2016) and supports HisR/TaHRC, about 50 kb from PFT. Placed at the cloned Fhb1 (TaHRC) position in the atlas. Read from the paper, Nov 2026 (ad39.py). Pangenome positions added Nov 2026 (ad64) with genome-wide gene anchors (106,795 Chinese Spring genes matched to each cultivar).

reports.name: Snn3-D1 (cloned; protein kinase-major sperm protein)
reports.note: Map-based cloning of Snn3-D1 from Ae. tauschii (TA2377 x AL8/78 population, BAC contig on AL8/78 scaffold 5289): the gene encodes protein kinase and major sperm protein domains, both essential for SnTox3 sensitivity; the interaction is light-independent and expression is down-regulated by light. Snn3-D1 likely arose in Ae. tauschii through a ~218-kb insertion along the west bank of the Caspian Sea; its homoeolog TaPKMSP-5B lies on 5B. Placed at the Snn3-D1 position in the atlas (Lin et al. 2021). Read from the paper, Nov 2026 (ad39.py). reports.name: QFhb.ifa-2A (Capo x Arina)
reports.note: FHB resistance (AUDPC, spray inoculation, 2011-2013) and anther retention in the Capo x Arina winter wheat population; MQM mapping on a DArT/SSR map. Flanking markers read from the LOD profiles in Online Resource 3 (Fig. S1); LOD and effect sizes from the main paper (not uploaded) are not entered. FHB QTL at the distal end of 2A (0-10 cM, wPt-7721 to wPt-8068), LOD about 5.5 in 2012 and above 3 for the mean. The SSRs on the same map orient it: Xgwm558 (about 33 cM) places at 361.2 Mb and Xgwm312/Xgwm294 (85 cM) at 709.0/716.5 Mb (in-silico PCR), so 0 cM is the distal end of 2AS. The QTL is therefore placed from the 2AS end to wPt-1657 (about 20 cM, 47.153 Mb, DArT tag BLAST); wPt-7721 (0 cM) places at 29.941 Mb. A 2012-only LOD peak near 40-45 cM is not entered. Read from Online Resource 3 (Fig. S1), Nov 2026 (ad40.py, ad42.py). Pangenome positions added Nov 2026 (ad64) with genome-wide gene anchors (106,795 Chinese Spring genes matched to each cultivar).

reports.name: QCr.3BL (Batavia/Ernie)
reports.note: Major QTL for crown rot resistance on 3BL in the Batavia/Ernie doubled-haploid population, resistance allele from Ernie; detected in all six seedling trials, three with F. graminearum CS3005 (LOD 3.3-6.1, R2 16.7-28.2%) and three with F. pseudograminearum CS3096 (LOD 4.3-7.6, R2 18.7-34.6%), interval 136.4-141.3 cM, closest marker wPt-1151. Not changed when plant height was fitted as a covariate (CR05-PH LOD 6.0, R2 27.5%; CR96-PH LOD 8.8, R2 35.8%). No other CR QTL detected; none of the FHB QTL coincides with it. wPt-1151 has no physical position; the interval is the RefSeq v1.0 span of the nearest placed map markers on either side, wPt-9368 (802.306 Mb) and wPt-1834 (815.459 Mb) (Figs 1-2 map order). Corrected from the paper, Nov 2026 (ad10.py). Pangenome positions added Nov 2026 (ad64) with genome-wide gene anchors (106,795 Chinese Spring genes matched to each cultivar).

reports.evidence: Results: Qcrs.cpi-3B flanked by wPt10505 and wPt2277; up to 49% (LOD 10.8); gwm0181 about 2.2 cM; validation 29-42% (mean 33%)
reports.marker: wPt10505, wPt2277 (flanking); gwm0181 (closest SSR, about 2.2 cM)
reports.name: Qcrs.cpi-3B (CSCR6)
reports.note: Major crown rot QTL on 3BL from the T. spelta accession CSCR6, flanked by DArT markers wPt10505 and wPt2277; detected with both F. pseudograminearum and F. graminearum isolates; up to 49% of phenotypic variance (LOD 10.8, interval mapping). Not co-located with known plant-height genes, but a strong interaction with Rht1 (4BS) was found; with Rht1 as cofactor the maximum effect fell to 43%. In four validation populations the QTL alone reduced crown rot severity by 29-42% (mean 33%). The flanking DArT markers have no physical position; the locus is placed at the RefSeq v1.0 position of gwm0181 (in-silico PCR), about 2.2 cM away. The same locus was later fine-mapped (see Qcrs.cpi-3B, Zheng et al.). Corrected from the paper, Nov 2026 (ad13.py). Pangenome positions added Nov 2026 (ad64) with genome-wide gene anchors (106,795 Chinese Spring genes matched to each cultivar).
reports.pve: up to 49 (43 with Rht1 as cofactor)

reports.name: qCR-6B
reports.note: Crown rot QTL in 168 durum wheat genotypes (DArTseq GWAS), field crown rot nursery at Warwick 2017; CR severity index from whitehead percentage and stem browning: five SNPs at 100.13-101.26 cM on the Svevo consensus map, peak 1023342 (-log10(P) 4.20). The same markers gave the whitehead QTL qWH1-6B (-log10(P) up to 3.88) and qWH2-6B (up to 3.58), and the yield QTL qGY-6B in the CR nursery. Haplotype hap1 gave 0.79 t/ha more yield under crown rot, a 4.24 d longer grain-filling period and higher root biomass; combined with qSRA-6A (root angle) the yield advantage was 0.90 t/ha. Positions are not printed in the paper; the interval is the RefSeq v1.0 span of the DArTseq tags placed by BLAST (4992135 668.534 Mb, 2254131 667.201 Mb, 2256390 674.327 Mb); 1023342 and 1039837 could not be placed. Corrected from the paper, Nov 2026 (ad14.py). Pangenome positions added Nov 2026 (ad64) with genome-wide gene anchors (106,795 Chinese Spring genes matched to each cultivar).

reports.name: QFhb 3A (Frontana x Remus)
reports.note: QTL for FHB resistance in the Frontana x Remus DH population (Tulln, Austria; spray and single-spikelet inoculation), resistance allele from Frontana. Detections: severity 3-year LOD 6.6 (16.2%), 1999 4.8 (12.0%), 2001 4.9 (12.1%), 2002 5.2 (12.9%); incidence 2002 LOD 4.6 (11.5%). The major QTL, described as near the centromere, most likely in the Xgwm720-Xdupw227 interval; not associated with spread; stable in all years. Lines with Frontana alleles at both 3A and 5A had about 40% less severity. Only Xdupw227 could be placed (598.979 Mb, Zhao et al. 2019 J Genet (Table S1)); position is that marker. This puts the locus on 3AL, not at the centromere as the paper describes; treat the position with care. No physical position printed. Corrected from the paper, Nov 2026 (ad21.py). Pangenome positions added Nov 2026 (ad64) with genome-wide gene anchors (106,795 Chinese Spring genes matched to each cultivar).
